sentences.text: The library doors opened at nine, and the room smelled like paper and polish.
The librarian rolled a cart of returned books to a sunny table.
One book showed whales diving under blue water.
Another book was full of maps of long rivers.
A visitor asked for a book that explained storms.
The librarian did not guess. She checked the computer, then walked to a shelf.
She pulled down a book with a dark cloud on the cover.
This one tells how thunder is made, she said.
The visitor smiled, chose a quiet chair, and opened to the first page.
A library works well when the people there know how to look things up.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A whale that swims into the library
A storm that closes the doors at nine
A visitor who already knows every shelf
A librarian finding the right book by looking it up

questions.explanation: The visitor asks about storms, and the librarian checks the computer and the shelf before choosing a book. Looking things up is the main idea.

questions.prompt: Returned books are books that people did what with?
questions.explanation: Returned means brought back. The librarian rolls a cart of books people have brought back to the library.

questions.prompt: What is on the cover of the storm book?
questions.explanation: The librarian pulls down a book with a dark cloud on the cover. The whale and the river maps are other books on the cart.
